Trip options between origin-destination pairs

Source: R/trip_options.R
trip_options.Rd

For each pair of origin and destination, every trip worth considering: the trips that no other trip beats on all the chosen criteria at once. This is a multi-criteria trip planner (see "Not dominated" and "Compared with the other functions" below).

Usage

trip_options(
  network,
  origins,
  destinations,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  mode_egress = "WALK",
  departure_datetime = NULL,
  time_window = 10L,
  criteria = NULL,
  max_walk_time = Inf,
  max_bike_time = Inf,
  max_car_time = Inf,
  max_trip_duration = 120L,
  walk_speed = 3.6,
  bike_speed = 12,
  max_rides = 3,
  max_lts = 2,
  fare_structure = NULL,
  max_fare = Inf,
  max_options = Inf,
  walk_resolution = 60L,
  all_to_all = FALSE,
  itineraries = TRUE,
  by_departure = FALSE,
  new_carspeeds = NULL,
  carspeed_scale = 1,
  new_lts = NULL,
  n_threads = Inf,
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE,
  drop_geometry = FALSE,
  osm_link_ids = FALSE,
  output_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network().

origins, destinations

A data.frame with columns id, lon and lat (WGS 84 longitude and latitude), or a POINT sf with an id column, in any coordinate reference system (CRS): an sf in another CRS than WGS 84 is reprojected with sf::st_transform(), with a message, and one without a CRS is an error. Ids that are not character are converted, with a warning; points with missing coordinates are not routed, with a warning; duplicated ids are an error.

mode

A character vector, the modes as in detailed_itineraries(); defaults to c("WALK", "TRANSIT"). Without a public transport mode the only option is the direct street trip.

mode_egress

A string, the mode from the last stop to the destination: "WALK" (the default), "BICYCLE" or "CAR". Ignored without public transport.

departure_datetime

A POSIXct, the departure date and time (see the section "Date and time"). Required with public transport.

time_window

An integer, the number of departure minutes, from departure_datetime on, over which travel times are computed. Defaults to 10.

criteria

A character vector, some of "TIME", "FARE", "TRANSFERS" and "WALK", or NULL (the default): all four with a fare_structure, all but "FARE" without one.

max_walk_time, max_bike_time, max_car_time

The maximum time in minutes on foot, by bicycle and by car. Each limit applies to each leg on its own (15 minutes to reach the first stop and another 15 from the last), and to the whole trip when that mode is the only one. Inf, the default, leaves only max_trip_duration.

max_trip_duration

An integer, the maximum trip duration in minutes. Defaults to 120.

walk_speed, bike_speed

Average speeds in km/h, 3.6 and 12 by default.

max_rides

An integer, the maximum number of public transport rides in a trip. Defaults to 3.

max_lts

An integer from 1 to 4, the highest level of traffic stress a cyclist rides on (see the section "Level of traffic stress"). Defaults to 2.

fare_structure

A fare structure (see setup_fare_structure()) or NULL (the default): no fares. It must have a row for every route of the network.

max_fare

A number, the highest fare of a trip (Inf, the default: no limit), in the currency of the fare structure; a finite value needs a fare_structure.

max_options

A number: at most this many options per pair, the first in the order of option; Inf (the default) for all of them.

walk_resolution

A number of seconds, 60 (the default): the step to which minutes on foot are compared. By default walking is compared to the whole minute (rounded), so that of two trips a few seconds of walking apart and otherwise no better only one is returned; 1 compares the exact seconds. See "Not dominated".

all_to_all

A logical. Whether to route from every origin to every destination (TRUE) or pair them row by row (FALSE, the default; a single origin or destination is repeated to match the other).

itineraries

A logical. Whether to build the legs of each option (TRUE, the default).

by_departure

A logical. Whether to add the options of every departure minute (FALSE, the default).

new_carspeeds

A scenario of car speeds: NULL (the default), a data frame with columns osm_id, max_speed and speed_type ("scale", a factor for the car speed of the way's edges, or "km/h", a speed; 0 closes the way to cars), or an sf data frame of POLYGONs or MULTIPOLYGONs (in any CRS, reprojected to WGS 84 as origins) with columns poly_id (character), scale (numeric) and priority (integer): each street edge takes the factor of the polygon it meets with the highest priority (ties: the one it overlaps most). Polygons that are not valid are an error, and so is a tie with no winner: two polygons of the same priority and different scales that overlap a way by the same length (give one of them a higher priority).

carspeed_scale

A number of at least 0, the factor for the car speeds of the edges new_carspeeds leaves out (all of them when it is NULL). Defaults to 1. Car speeds are kept as 16-bit centimetres per second: a factor or speed that would bring a speed to 0 or less, or past that range, is an error.

new_lts

A scenario of levels of traffic stress: NULL (the default), a data frame with columns osm_id and lts (integer), or an sf data frame of LINESTRINGs (in any CRS, reprojected to WGS 84 as origins) with columns line_id, lts (1 to 4) and priority: each street edge takes the level of the line closest to it among those whose bounding box meets its own (priority is not used). A scenario (of car speeds or of levels of traffic stress) changes the street search from the origins (the trip without public transport, and access by bicycle or car) but not the egress from the stops, and turns off slope costs, with a warning, on a network built with an elevation raster.

n_threads

The number of threads; Inf (the default) uses all cores (two under R CMD check when it limits the cores).

verbose, progress

Logicals, checked but without effect: no progress counter or routing log is printed.

drop_geometry

A logical. Whether to leave the geometry of the legs out (and return them as a table without geometry).

osm_link_ids

A logical. Whether to add the columns osm_id_list (the OpenStreetMap way ids of a street leg's edges), edge_id_list (the indices of the street network's edges, as street_network_to_sf() numbers them), both as "[id1, id2, ...]" and "[]" for rides, and board_stop_id, alight_stop_id (a ride's stops, "<feed>:<stop_id>"; empty for street legs). Consecutive edges on a roundabout give only their first ids, and connectors none. Needs drop_geometry = FALSE. Defaults to FALSE.

output_dir

NULL or a directory: write one CSV file per pair with options, from_<origin id>_to_<destination id>.csv, one row per leg (or per option, with itineraries = FALSE) with the option's and the leg's columns and the geometry as WKT, and return output_dir.

Value

A list with

  • options, a table: one row per option, with from_id, to_id, option (from 1, ordered by total time, then fare, transfers and minutes on foot), total_time (minutes, one decimal place), fare (with a fare_structure), transfers, walk_time (minutes), departure_time and arrival_time of the option's best minute, n_departures, first_departure, last_departure and description (the modes and route short names, as "WALK > BUS 343 > WALK");

  • itineraries (with itineraries = TRUE): the legs of each option at its best minute, in the format of detailed_itineraries() and keyed by from_id, to_id and option: segment, mode, cumulative_fare (with a fare_structure), segment_duration, wait, distance, route, the four id columns with osm_link_ids, and the geometry: an sf of LINESTRINGs in EPSG:4326, or a table without geometry with drop_geometry = TRUE;

  • departures (with by_departure = TRUE), a table: for every departure minute, the options on its frontier (from_id, to_id, option, departure_time, arrival_time, total_time).

Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package). An sf result keeps its geometry column and EPSG:4326 and takes the same data frame class: an sf tibble, a plain sf data frame, or, with "data.table", an sf data.table where the section "Class of the results" of peabiru-package says so. With "data.table", the itineraries are an sf data.table, as those of detailed_itineraries().

Not dominated

A trip dominates another when it is no worse on every chosen criterion and better on at least one. The criteria are

  • "TIME": door-to-door minutes from the departure minute, waits included;

  • "FARE": the fare by fare_structure (needs one);

  • "TRANSFERS": rides minus one; a trip without public transport has 0, as many as a trip with a single ride;

  • "WALK": minutes on foot, that is the access and egress legs when they are walked and the walks between stops. A bicycle or car leg counts 0, also where the cyclist pushes the bicycle.

At each departure minute of the window (departure_datetime, plus one minute at a time for time_window minutes) the options are the exact set of trips not dominated, one trip per combination of values: of trips with the same values on the chosen criteria, the one with the least total time, then transfers, minutes on foot and fare is kept. Trips are built as in the other routing functions, so that their times agree with detailed_itineraries(): a direct trip by the street mode, and trips that reach a stop of the access search, ride and walk between stops (the transfers of the other functions), and leave a stop of the egress search; each ride boards at least a minute after its stop is reached, on the vehicle that gets to the alighting stop first.

The search is exact; what is returned is then compared at the resolution the values are read at: total time to a tenth of a minute (as it is reported), and minutes on foot to the whole minute (rounded, walk_resolution seconds). Of the trips of a minute's exact set, one is left out when another is no worse on every criterion in those terms and better on one, or equal on all and better in exact terms (least total time, then transfers, walking, fare); two trips a few seconds of walking apart are not both returned. The values returned are exact. Rounding cannot make a trip look better than one that beats it, so this is the same as comparing every trip at that resolution.

The minutes are then merged into options: trips with the same street modes, the same routes between the same stops (whichever vehicles), and the same fare, transfers and minutes on foot are one option, available at n_departures minutes from first_departure to last_departure. Its total time changes with the minute (the wait at the start does); the option reports the trip of its best minute, the one with the least total time (the earliest of equal ones). With by_departure = TRUE the result also has every minute's options.

Frequency-based routes (GTFS frequencies.txt) are boarded at their expected times: half a headway after the boarding wait (or after the start of the period), within the period; with exact_times = 1 at the first scheduled departure. There are no random draws and no seed, and the results differ on purpose from the Monte Carlo draws of the other routing functions.

Fares

Fares follow fare_structure exactly as pareto_frontier() and detailed_itineraries() compute them (in cents). A fare is not the sum of its rides (discounted transfers within a time allowance, unlimited transfers, a cap), so two partial trips are only compared on fare when one is at least as cheap for every way both can continue; the comparison makes no assumption about the structure. This is what makes fare criteria slower than the others: trips waiting for a discount are kept apart until they cannot get one any more.

Compared with the other functions

pareto_frontier() gives, for each fare cutoff, the percentiles of the travel time over Monte Carlo draws of departure times; detailed_itineraries() gives the fastest trip, or with shortest_path = FALSE the alternatives, one per sequence of routes. trip_options() gives the trade-offs themselves: the trips that are faster, cheaper, with fewer transfers or less walking than the others, each with its legs. With criteria = "TIME" and time_window = 1 its first option has the total time of detailed_itineraries()'s fastest trip.

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))

trips <- trip_options(
  network, points[10, ], points[12, ],
  departure_datetime = as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00",
                                  tz = "America/Sao_Paulo"),
  n_threads = 2
)
trips$options
#> # A tibble: 4 × 12
#>   from_id         to_id     option total_time transfers walk_time departure_time
#>   <chr>           <chr>      <int>      <dbl>     <int>     <dbl> <chr>         
#> 1 89a8100c037ffff 89a8100c…      1       31.8         0      26.1 14:00:00      
#> 2 89a8100c037ffff 89a8100c…      2       34.3         1      22.4 14:00:00      
#> 3 89a8100c037ffff 89a8100c…      3       34.7         0      24.2 14:00:00      
#> 4 89a8100c037ffff 89a8100c…      4       34.9         0      19.7 14:00:00      
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: arrival_time <chr>, n_departures <int>,
#> #   first_departure <chr>, last_departure <chr>, description <chr>
